title: Monk is fired at the Apollo and John Lewis takes over the piano
summary: Late back from the Braddock Bar, Clarke slipped onto the drums and was fined; Monk was fired in the wings and John Lewis became Dizzy's pianist.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: So, well, we worked around a little bit, you know, and John was coming along with the band. Sometimes he would stay in New York and so forth. So one day we played the Apollo Theater. So Monk and I went to the Braddock Bar to

have a drink during the half hour, you know. So we were there, drinking beer and talking and laughing. So I looked at my watch, I said, "Oh, my God, Monk, we missed the half hour." And he said, "Oh, oh." So some way I said, "We better get out of here." He said, "Yeah, we better." So we ran backstage and there was Milt Jackson, sitting up on the drums, but behind the curtain I sneaked up under the curtain and sneaked up on the stand, I said, "Bags, hey Bags." So Bags, he said, "Is that you, Klook Klunk?" I said, "Yeah. Let me get up. Let me get up." He said, "Okay, okay." So he gave me the sticks and I climbed up on the drums and Bags climbed down, and when Diz looked up, there I was, playing. So he looked at me and said -- so I just kept playing. "Yeah, man, here we go." You know. So Monk walked in behind me to the piano. So before he could sit down, he was coming through the wings -- before he could sit down, Dizzy looked at him and pointed. He said, "And you, you're fired." But he fined me $25.00, which Lorraine said, "No, give Kenny his money. No, don't do that." "Because he was there playing and he did not miss the show. All he missed was the theme song."
Lorraine's nice like that.

Yeah. She said, "Give Kenny his money." $28.00 he fined me. But Monk, he said, "You're fired." So John Lewis was sitting in the wings, and so Dizzy just beckoned, he said, "John." And John came to play the --
Diz was real mad, then.

Oh, he was mad with Monk, because Monk, he comes in like he missed the whole thing. I don't know why he was waiting out there. Because no-one was at the piano, so he could have sneaked in easily, more easily than I did, you know. But he just stood in the wings, wanted to be grand, you know, and Dizzy just pointed and said, "You're fired." And John Lewis came right in and sat down with the piano, and there it was. He was the pianist from then on.
Fancy that.
And Monk was our pianist.
So this was how John's career got launched.

Uh-huh. And John, he used to want to do something for me, you know. He said, "What can I do?" I said nothing, nothing. He said, "Do you need money?" I said, "No, I don't need a thing." You know? Everything is beautiful.
That was nice.
He couldn't get over it, you know.
Yeah.
When I said, "Well, it's your talent, you know."
Yeah.
I just happened to find a place to place
it, you know. So make the best of it you can.
Yeah.
So then he never looked back. He just kept going on.
That was wonderful.
Which is beautiful.
Yeah.
